results.title: Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis: 2017 revisions of the McDonald criteria
results.authors: Thompson AJ, Banwell BL, Barkhof F, et al.
results.summary: The 2017 McDonald criteria require demonstration of dissemination in space (DIS) and dissemination in time (DIT) for MS diagnosis. DIS requires one or more T2 lesions in at least 2 of 4 characteristic regions: periventricular, cortical/juxtacortical, infratentorial, and spinal cord. DIT can be satisfied by simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions, a new T2/enhancing lesion on follow-up MRI, or the presence of CSF-specific oligoclonal bands. The updated criteria allow oligoclonal bands to substitute for DIT when DIS is met.

results.title: Late-onset multiple sclerosis: clinical features, diagnostic challenges, and disease course
results.authors: Kis B, Rumberg B, Berlit P
results.summary: Late-onset MS (first symptom after age 50) accounts for approximately 1-10% of all MS cases. The clinical presentation frequently differs from younger-onset MS: a myelopathic onset is more common, cerebellar symptoms are frequent, the relapsing-remitting course can be present but is harder to identify, and the differential with vascular leukoencephalopathy is more challenging. Careful morphologic assessment of lesion characteristics — particularly juxtacortical location, Dawson fingers pattern, and cord involvement — along with CSF oligoclonal bands, is critical to reaching the correct diagnosis.

results.title: Multiple sclerosis
results.authors: Reich DS, Lucchinetti CF, Calabresi PA
results.summary: Comprehensive review covering RRMS diagnosis, pathophysiology, and treatment. Key distinguishing features of MS lesions from small-vessel ischemic lesions include: periventricular Dawson fingers, juxtacortical involvement, infratentorial and spinal cord predilection, CSF oligoclonal bands (present in ~95% of MS), and the temporal pattern of relapsing attacks. Disease-modifying therapy options range from platform agents (interferon-beta, glatiramer acetate, dimethyl fumarate, teriflunomide) to high-efficacy agents (natalizumab, ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, cladribine, siponimod).

results.title: MRI criteria for the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis: MAGNIMS consensus guidelines
results.authors: Filippi M, Rocca MA, Ciccarelli O, et al.
results.summary: MAGNIMS guidelines specify that periventricular lesions should number 3 or more to meet that criterion for DIS; lesions adjacent to the body of the lateral ventricles, perpendicular orientation (Dawson fingers), and involvement of infratentorial/cord regions are distinguishing features. Non-specific WMH in subcortical and deep white matter due to small-vessel disease tend to be rounded, more symmetric, and lack juxtacortical and cord involvement.

output.summary: Late-onset MS (first symptom after age 50) presents diagnostic challenges because vascular risk factors and non-specific white matter hyperintensities are common in this age group. The 2017 McDonald criteria remain applicable; characteristic lesion morphology (Dawson fingers, juxtacortical involvement, infratentorial, cord) combined with CSF oligoclonal bands provides the diagnostic foundation. AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG must be excluded. Spinal cord involvement argues against pure small-vessel ischemic disease, which does not typically cause short-segment eccentric cord lesions.

interactions: Metformin + dimethyl fumarate: No clinically significant interaction; monitor renal function as both drugs depend on renal clearance.

Atorvastatin + fingolimod: No significant pharmacokinetic interaction; however, fingolimod is associated with first-dose bradyarrhythmia requiring baseline ECG and 6-hour cardiac monitoring — flagged for completeness.
Amlodipine + fingolimod: Additive bradycardic effect possible — caution if fingolimod selected.
Hydrochlorothiazide: No significant interactions with major MS DMTs.
contraindications: Natalizumab: contraindicated if JC virus antibody index is high (PML risk); JCV serostatus must be obtained before initiation.
Fingolimod: requires first-dose monitoring (bradyarrhythmia); baseline ophthalmology evaluation recommended to screen for macular edema; avoid in patients with significant cardiac conduction disease.
Cladribine: requires complete blood count and lymphocyte count monitoring; contraindicated in active infection and severe hepatic or renal impairment.
warnings: With diabetes mellitus on metformin: if natalizumab or ocrelizumab is selected, monitor for infections including urinary tract infections (greater UTI susceptibility in diabetics on immunomodulating therapy).
Ocrelizumab (anti-CD20): requires hepatitis B screening before initiation; live vaccines must be completed at least 4 weeks prior.
Dimethyl fumarate: GI side effects common initially; monitor CBC for lymphopenia (risk of PML if prolonged severe lymphopenia <500 cells/microL for >6 months).
JC virus serostatus should be assessed before natalizumab; if JCV antibody positive with index >0.9, risk-benefit discussion required.
All B-cell depleting or S1P modulator DMTs: live-attenuated vaccines must not be administered after initiation.

sequence_constraints.reason: Standard pre-LP imaging: confirm absence of mass effect or herniation risk on brain MRI before lumbar puncture

critical_actions: Establish dissemination in space (DIS) using brain and spinal-cord MRI: confirm lesions in at least 2 of 4 MS-typical regions (periventricular, juxtacortical/cortical, infratentorial, spinal cord)

Establish dissemination in time (DIT): the simultaneously enhancing cerebellar peduncle lesion and non-enhancing periventricular lesions satisfy DIT on a single MRI; confirm this on the brain MRI before proceeding

Identify MS-typical lesion morphology (Dawson fingers perpendicular to ventricles, juxtacortical U-fiber involvement, infratentorial and cord lesions) to distinguish from the non-specific deep WMH attributable to small-vessel disease
Perform lumbar puncture after brain MRI confirms no mass effect — CSF oligoclonal bands are the critical adjudicator between MS demyelination and hypertensive leukoencephalopathy
Exclude NMOSD and MOGAD with AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG cell-based assays before committing to MS diagnosis and selecting a DMT
Recognize that Lhermitte sign, unilateral RAPD with disc pallor, and spinal cord lesions are not features of small-vessel ischemic disease and strongly raise the pre-test probability of MS
Treat the acute relapse with high-dose IV methylprednisolone (1 g daily for 3-5 days) once the diagnosis is established
Initiate a disease-modifying therapy (DMT) after stabilization; in this patient with diabetes and hypertension, consider infection risk when selecting immunosuppressive DMTs
Check JC virus antibody serostatus before considering natalizumab
Address modifiable cardiovascular risk factors (optimize BP, LDL, HbA1c) independent of MS management — these contribute to white matter disease burden
contraindicated_actions: Do not attribute the full white matter lesion burden to small-vessel ischemic disease based on vascular risk factor profile alone — lesion morphology (Dawson fingers, juxtacortical, infratentorial, cord) and CSF OCBs must be sought
Do not diagnose MS without meeting McDonald 2017 criteria and excluding mimics — age >50 at first presentation mandates a more stringent mimic exclusion workup
Do not start natalizumab without first obtaining JC virus antibody serostatus (PML risk)
Do not initiate fingolimod without baseline ECG and 6-hour first-dose cardiac monitoring; exercise particular caution given concurrent amlodipine (additive bradycardic risk)
Do not use chronic oral corticosteroids as MS maintenance therapy
Do not administer live-attenuated vaccines after initiation of B-cell depleting or S1P modulator DMTs
Do not omit spinal cord MRI — cord lesions are critical evidence against pure small-vessel disease and contribute to DIS

Do not misattribute the prior right-arm tingling (14 months ago) and transient left monocular visual blur (8 months ago) to radiculopathy and hypertensive retinopathy without re-evaluating them as prior demyelinating attacks that establish disease chronicity
key_reasoning_points: Late-onset MS (first symptom >50 years) is a diagnostic puzzle because multiple vascular risk factors and non-specific WMH are expected in this age group — the trap is anchoring on small-vessel ischemic disease and never reaching the MS diagnosis

MS-typical morphology resolves the ambiguity: periventricular lesions with Dawson fingers (ovoid, perpendicular to ventricles on sagittal FLAIR), juxtacortical U-fiber involvement, infratentorial enhancement, and short-segment eccentric cord lesions are not features of hypertensive leukoencephalopathy

Spinal cord involvement is the pivotal discriminator — small-vessel ischemic disease does not cause short-segment, eccentric, enhancing intramedullary cord lesions; their presence in this case argues decisively against a purely vascular etiology

CSF oligoclonal bands (6 CSF-restricted bands, IgG index 0.82) confirm intrathecal IgG synthesis — present in ~95% of MS but absent in small-vessel ischemic disease; this is the key biochemical adjudicator

Lhermitte sign (Lhermitte phenomenon) — electric shock on neck flexion radiating into the limbs — indicates a lesion in the posterior cervical cord and is not a feature of vascular WMH or radiculopathy

The prior episodes (right arm tingling 14 months ago, transient left monocular visual blur 8 months ago with disc pallor and RAPD) represent previous demyelinating attacks misattributed to radiculopathy and hypertensive retinopathy — recognizing these establishes chronicity and a relapsing course
Left optic nerve involvement (RAPD, disc pallor, reduced RNFL on OCT, markedly prolonged P100 latency on VEP) corroborates prior subclinical optic neuritis and contributes to DIS

McDonald 2017 criteria are satisfied: DIS achieved across periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, and spinal cord regions; DIT achieved by simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions on brain MRI

Mildly elevated homocysteine, borderline B12, dyslipidemia, and elevated HbA1c are genuine vascular risk factors that co-exist with MS and should be managed independently — but they do not explain the demyelinating lesion morphology and CSF profile
Choice of DMT must account for diabetes-related infection risk, the additive bradycardic effect of amlodipine with fingolimod, and JCV serostatus before natalizumab selection

red_herrings.data_point: Low-normal vitamin B12 at 224 pg/mL and right lower extremity sensory loss with extensor plantar response, raising concern for subacute combined degeneration
red_herrings.intended_effect: An agent may pursue B12 deficiency myelopathy as the explanation for the right-sided myelopathic signs (sensory loss, hyperreflexia, Babinski), especially in an older patient with low-normal B12 — delaying MS workup
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: B12 at 224 pg/mL is low-normal but not in the frank deficiency range that causes subacute combined degeneration; moreover, SCD causes symmetric bilateral dorsal column-predominant cord lesions and does not explain periventricular Dawson fingers, infratentorial active enhancement, juxtacortical lesion, or CSF OCBs

metadata.condition_name: Late-onset relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (first presentation age 54)
metadata.real_seed_note: Web search for a verifiable open-access PMC late-onset RRMS case (first presentation >50 yo, small-vessel disease differential, confirmed RRMS with OCBs) did not return a verifiable PMID during authoring. This case is authored de novo by the condition expert following the real-seeding policy: clinical scenario, demographics, symptom course, and lab/imaging values are constructed to reflect authentic late-onset RRMS epidemiology as documented in the cited literature (Reich 2018, McDonald 2017, Kis 2008 J Neurol). The case is clinically authentic and does not require a seed PMID to be valid.
metadata.difficulty_description: Diagnostic puzzle: a 54-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and smoking history presents with a right myelopathic syndrome. Multiple vascular risk factors and non-specific deep WMH anchor strongly toward small-vessel ischemic leukoencephalopathy. The agent must recognize MS-typical lesion morphology (Dawson fingers, juxtacortical, infratentorial, cord), elicit the significance of Lhermitte sign and prior misattributed attacks, obtain CSF OCBs as the biochemical adjudicator, exclude NMOSD/MOGAD, and reach RRMS as the correct diagnosis.
case_body_concerns: Mock-server note: This case has two distinct order_specialized_test calls in the gold trajectory (optical_coherence_tomography at step 7 and vep at step 8). The mock server resolves order_specialized_test to a single output slot keyed by test_type. The followup_outputs stores these as separate FollowUpToolOutput entries with distinct trigger_actions ('request_oct' and 'request_vep'). The evaluation harness should serve the OCT output for trigger_action 'request_oct' and the VEP output for trigger_action 'request_vep'. This is consistent with the pattern used in MS-RR-RP03 and MS-RR-RS04.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required tools, 3 embedded red herrings (vascular risk factor cluster, non-specific WMH with radiologist hedge toward ischemia, low-normal B12 with myelopathy), Lhermitte sign and prior misattributed attacks require active synthesis, OCBs are the critical adjudicator

fallback_tool_kinds.echo: mild hypertensive changes, no cardioembolic source
fallback_tool_kinds.cardiac_monitoring: sinus rhythm, rare PACs, no AF
